key_insight: Twins unifies multimodal understanding and image generation by learning a single continuous token space instead of forcing separate semantic and synthesis representations. It does this by combining ViT and VAE features and training them with focal loss to make the shared space more reliable.
problem_solved: Existing unified multimodal systems often split understanding and generation into mismatched latent spaces: semantic ViT features for comprehension and VAE latents for synthesis. This mismatch makes it difficult to use one representation for both tasks.
method: Channel-wise concatenate ViT semantic features and VAE low-level latents into a unified continuous token representation.
Train the shared token space with focal loss to emphasize hard-to-predict tokens and improve alignment across modalities.
Use the unified representation as a common interface for both multimodal understanding and image generation.
impact: This approach can simplify multimodal model design by reducing the gap between understanding and generation pipelines. For practitioners, it offers a more coherent representation that may improve transfer, consistency, and efficiency in unified AI systems.

paper_title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
paper_authors: Kaixiong Gong, Xin Cai, Bin Lin, Hao Wang, Yunlong Lin
